h: Holy Intention Brings Divine Presence Into Our Deeds

p: and I invite to it now
and the table with the bread," etc.
Even though the menorah and the table
the arranging of the table in the north
and the menorah in the south,
so what is the expression "I will arrange"?
and from this the supernal light shines
"a new table and a fine menorah."
when the table is not new,
for the table was set since yesterday,
"and I invite to it now Atika Kadisha"?
"This is the meal of Atika Kadisha."
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
based on what is written in the holy Zohar
(פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, חֵלֶק ג נא סוֹף עַמּוּד ב)
(on this parshah, III 51, end of amud b):
In all of a person's deeds
that they all be for the holy Name.
To mention the holy Name with his mouth
that all is for His service," etc.
This implies that it refers to a person's deeds
that he must mention over them
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ם זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
along the lines of what the Rambam, of blessed memory, wrote
"And let all your deeds be for the sake of Heaven" (Avos 2:12):
that if a person has the intention
for the sake of Heaven in bodily matters,
כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ כֹּחַ לִלְמוֹד תּוֹרָה
so that he have strength to learn Torah,
then this deed is a mitzvah;
and likewise when he engages in commerce,
he should mention that he does it for the sake of Heaven,
so that he can set times for Torah study
and raise his children to Torah study.
וְכֵן נִרְאֶה מִלְּשׁוֹן הַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (נ, א)
And so it appears from the language of the holy Zohar (III 50a),
"And therefore one who builds a building,
that it is for the service of HaKadosh Baruch Hu
'Woe to him who builds his house, etc.'"
to refer to an optional building.
מַה וּפָקַדְתָּ נָוְךָ כוּ׳ (אִיּוֹב ה, כד)
"What is 'And you shall visit your dwelling,' etc. (Iyov 5:24)?
To deposit a word in the mouth
and then 'and you shall not sin' is written," etc.
And although we find, regarding the eternal House
that he certainly mentioned the Name of Heaven
over every work of the Mikdash,
that he set up an idol in the Heichal,
and likewise all that is mentioned in Yechezkel (chapter 8)
that was done in the Beis HaMikdash
it appears that the intent of the holy Zohar
in writing "and you shall not sin"
is that the thing not cause sin.
For regarding optional eating it is written (Devarim 11:15-16):
"And you will eat and be satisfied.
for the yetzer hara has dominion
as they said in the Sifrei
and build fine houses and dwell in them, etc.,
and your heart grow haughty and you forget, etc."
And about this it says in the holy Zohar:
"to deposit a word in the mouth":
for when he mentions the Name of Heaven
over the building or the eating
that he does with intention for the sake of Heaven,
that he have room for Torah and prayer
or to raise his children to Torah study,
then the building will not bring him
to the accusation of the yetzer hara.
And as it says in the holy Zohar earlier:
וְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא זָמִין עֲלֵיהּ קְדוּשָּׁתָא
and HaKadosh Baruch Hu prepares holiness for him
'And you shall know that your tent is at peace.'"
That is, that there be peace
from the accusation of the yetzer hara,
which is the essence of peace;
and as they said (in Bereishis Rabbah 54):
גַּם אוֹיְבָיו יַשְׁלִים אִתּוֹ (מִשְׁלֵי טז, ז)
He makes even his enemies at peace with him' (Mishlei 16:7)
and as they said (Toras Kohanim, Bechukosai):
if there is no peace, there is nothing;
'And I will give peace in the land,
and you will lie down with none to make you afraid.'"
For without this he is afraid
of the agitation of the yetzer hara,
And for this is the promise,
from the accusation of the yetzer hara;
and then none makes him afraid of its agitation.
וְאַף דִּבְזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (לְקַמָּן עַמּוּד ב) אִיתָא
And although in the holy Zohar (further on, amud b) it is stated:
"Once all has been purified and cleansed,
how then does the verse conclude,
"and your heart grow haughty and you forget"?
And it appears that it refers to what is said (Devarim 8:13):
"And your cattle and your flocks increase,
and silver and gold increase for you, etc.";
and about this it says "and your heart grow haughty."
For so too what it says,
of one who does not recite Birkas HaMazon
And regarding one who recites Birkas HaMazon it is written (Devarim 8:10):
"And you will eat and be satisfied and bless,"
and there it does not say
"beware for yourselves lest it be enticed."
what it says, "and your heart grow haughty,"
refers to the pasuk "and your cattle, etc."
וְכֵן נִרְאֶה מִמַּה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחַר כָּךְ
And so it appears from what is said afterward (Devarim 8:17):
'My strength and the might of my hand
עָשָׂה לִי אֶת הַחַיִל הַזֶּה וְגוֹ׳
cattle and flocks and silver and gold,
and not to eating and building;
and as is written in the Targum:
קְנוֹ לִי יָת נִכְסַיָּא הָאִלֵּין וְכוּלֵּי
וְאָמַר שֶׁכְּשֶׁמַּזְכִּיר שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם עַל הַדָּבָר
And it says that when he mentions the Name of Heaven over the matter,
אָז אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא אוֹתוֹ לִידֵי חֵטְא
then it does not bring him to sin.

p: all this concerns an optional building
but with eating that is a mitzvah
and building that is a mitzvah,
it would appear that one need not mention
that he does it for the sake of Heaven,
since as a matter of course it is a mitzvah act.
But from what is written in the holy Zohar
וְכָל הַנָּשִׁים אֲשֶׁר נָשָׂא לִבָּן וְגוֹ׳
'And all the women whose heart lifted them, etc.'
when they were doing the work,
this is for the Paroches,' etc.,
בְּגִין דְּתִשְׁרֵי קְדִישָׁא עַל יְדַיְיהוּ כוּ׳
so that holiness would rest upon their hands," etc.
that even in the mitzvah acts
he must mention with his mouth
that he does it for the sake of Heaven,
so that holiness rest upon it.
For what is greater for us
than the making of the Mishkan,
the intention for the sake of Heaven.
And in truth this is explicit in the parshah,
for the work of the Tent of Meeting
and for the holy garments, etc.";
who waved a waving of gold to Hashem";
for the Efod and for the Choshen, etc.,
for the light and for the anointing oil
and for the incense of spices, etc." (35:27-28).
And why did the verse specify
Would we not know by ourselves
that the stones were for the Efod and the Choshen,
and the spice and the oil
for the light and the anointing oil and the incense?
And likewise after this it says (35:29):
"The Children of Israel brought a free-will offering to Hashem."
And in the Torah there is not written,
So perforce it comes to teach us
that at the time of bringing,
each one of Yisrael would mention
the purpose of the bringing, for the sake of Heaven,
to do the work of the Mishkan,
and likewise for each and every detail,
in order to mention the Name of Heaven
and therefore it mentions "a free-will offering to Hashem,"
as is written in the holy Zohar.
And although it is stated in the Gemara (Zevachim 2b):
that one should not say 'for its sake,'
lest he come to say 'not for its sake'";
and although among the six things
for which the offering is slaughtered
is counted "for the sake of the Name,"
and from this the Noda BiYehudah
(מַהֲדוּרָא קַמָּא חֵלֶק יוֹרֶה דֵּעָה סִימָן צג)
proof that one need not say
"for the sake of the union," etc.
perhaps it is specifically the kohanim,
who are the agents of the Merciful One,
and the act is not on their own account
who need not mention the intention with the mouth,
for as a matter of course it is done
for the sake of Hashem who sends them,
since an agent carries out his agency;
that they not mention with their mouths "for the sake of Hashem";
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִי שֶׁהֵבִיא נִדְבָתוֹ
which is not so with one who brought his donation,
or the craftsmen who made the work,
for this was only from the generosity of their hearts.
And likewise everyone who does a mitzvah
rightly must mention the Name of Heaven
over the act that he does,
so that the Shechinah and holiness rest
upon the work of his hands;
and as is written in the holy Zohar:
and when it goes up to its place,

p: וְכָל הַנָּשִׁים אֲשֶׁר נָשָׂא לִבָּן אוֹתָנָה
"And all the women whose heart lifted them
and there it does not mention at all
that they said the intention with their mouths,
that the intent of the holy Zohar
is that saying is not enough,
rather wisdom of the heart is also needed
to bring holiness into the act;
and as it says of Betzalel (Shemos 31:3):
"And I filled him with the spirit of God,
with which heaven and earth were created," etc.
"And in the heart of every wise-hearted one
And why did they need this?
Was the Mishkan not a work of holiness,
and it would have been enough
for the craftsmen to do their work,
and the holiness would come by itself?
But it appears that it was necessary
that each one bring holiness into his deeds.
And this is the matter of what it writes (Shemos 35:25):
וְכָל אִשָּׁה חַכְמַת לֵב בְּיָדֶיהָ טָווּ
"And every wise-hearted woman spun with her hands,
and they brought the spun blue wool, etc."
And why did it mention "wise-hearted" in this?
that every woman does for her husband?
who was able to bring holiness into her deeds,
And this is what they said (in Shabbos 99a):
"Greater is the wisdom stated regarding the upper curtains
than that stated regarding the lower ones, etc.;
whereas regarding the upper ones it is written:
וְכָל הַנָּשִׁים אֲשֶׁר נָשָׂא לִבָּן אוֹתָנָה
'And all the women whose heart lifted them
and it was taught in the name of Rabbi Nechemiah:
it was washed on the goats,
and they spun it from the goats."
And in truth, why did they do so?
That is not the normal way of spinning,
And why did they need to act with extraordinary wisdom,
not in the normal way of spinning,
and not from detached wool, in the normal way of spinning?
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמַר הָאֲרִ״י הַקָּדוֹשׁ
based on what the holy Ari said
I, neither in my poverty did I eat vegetables,
in my poverty, because they whet the appetite;
in my wealth, because I said:
And Heaven forbid that Rav Chisda
one can extract more holy sparks
than one can extract from plants.
And he said, "not in my poverty"
that is, at the time he was poor in understanding
for it is hard to extract from there
and one could be further corrupted, Heaven forbid,
שֶׁמִּשָּׁם יֵשׁ יוֹתֵר נִיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת לְהוֹצִיא
for from there there are more holy sparks to extract.
And one may interpret the intent:
for He apportions to him as much
as he needs for Torah and service.
And we find with Rav Nachman,
and a son-in-law of the Nasi's house,
"As long as I have not drunk
הַיְינוּ שֶׁכֵּיוָן שֶׁנָּתַן לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
That is, since Hashem Yisbarach gave him
that is, for Torah and service,
and that is his allotted bread.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And as we find with King Shlomo, alav hashalom,
וּבִיקֵּשׁ הַטְרִיפֵנִי לֶחֶם חוּקִּי (מִשְׁלֵי ל, ח)
and he asked, "Provide me my allotted bread" (Mishlei 30:8),
שֶׁכָּל זֶה הָיָה נִקְרָא לֶחֶם חוּקִּי
for all of this was called "my allotted bread."
And this is what Rav Chisda said,
"in my wealth," when he became wealthy;
וּמִן הַסְּתָם הָיָה נִצְרָךְ לוֹ הָעוֹשֶׁר
and presumably he needed the wealth,
and he was rich in understanding,
and this is what he said,
And so is the matter here:
to extract the holiness from living creatures.
And this is the matter of what is mentioned,
and the Rishonim did not explain its matter.
And it appears that it is
בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (פָּרָשָׁה טו, ג)
in Midrash Rabbah on this parshah (Vayikra Rabbah 15:3):
מִי פִלַּג לַשֶּׁטֶף תְּעָלָה (אִיּוֹב לח, כה)
"'Who has cleft a channel for the torrent?' (Iyov 38:25)
שֶׁלֹּא בָּרָא בָּהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
for which HaKadosh Baruch Hu did not create
a follicle of its own," etc.
And this is "washed on the goats":
they would no longer have been able
to extract the life force and the holiness
for then it is like inanimate matter, detached;
for each hair had a follicle
that draws from the living creature,
and they spun on the goats;
and through this they were able
to extract the holiness and the life force
and this is the extraordinary wisdom
that they spoke of in the Gemara.
And this is "greater is the wisdom," etc.,
as it says, "whose heart lifted them
who "spun with her hands" from detached wool,
to bring holiness into their deeds as they did.
of why the holy Zohar brings the pasuk,
וְכָל הַנָּשִׁים אֲשֶׁר נָשָׂא לִבָּן וְגוֹ׳
"And all the women whose heart lifted them, etc.":
that one must bring holiness in
even when doing a mitzvah act.
even one who does not have the power
to bring holiness in with the heart
must mention it with the mouth;
'This is for the Sanctuary, this is for the Paroches.'"
And they brought the holiness in with the heart;
one must mention with the mouth
the Name of Heaven over the deed.
regarding every building that one builds,
that he should mention that he does it for the sake of Heaven
and that he builds for the service of HaKadosh Baruch Hu;
and likewise to mention the holy Name
that all of it is for His service;
that has in it intention for the sake of Heaven
as the Rambam, of blessed memory, wrote.
And this is the matter of what we say,
that is, that it is a mitzvah meal,
which Chazal learned from the three times "today"
"and I invite to it now Atika Kadisha"
אוֹמְרִים גַּם כֵּן בַּפֶּה עַל כָּל פָּנִים
we also say with the mouth, at least,
that one invites the holiness of this meal,
which is the meal of Atika.
And regarding Shabbos it is written (Yeshayahu 58:13):
that on Shabbos one can speak
so that it be called the word of Hashem;
and as is written in the holy Zohar
יֵשׁ לוֹ גַּם כֵּן כֹּחַ גָּדוֹל
more than on the other days;
and the more that a person is able
to bring into the Shabbos meal
